lines.text: Something shipped on Friday, and your team has one question. Who approved the deploy?
Nobody knows, because the team shares one agent setup and one login.
Agent R Q gives each workspace its own private Slack channel. Only the people you add can see it.
Create a task with slash t, right inside the channel. Maya reports a rounding bug.
It creates the task, assigns it to the coding agent, and the agent starts work.
Reply in the thread with an at mention of Agent R Q, and your message goes to the agent.
When the agent needs permission, the approval lands in that thread. Anyone on the team can answer.
Sam taps allow once, and it is saved under his own name.
Every decision is attributed to a person. Sam approved the push, and Maya denied a risky delete.
No shared login to rotate, and no extra seats to buy.
So next time something ships on a Friday, you open the log and read a name.
Give your team its own channel and its own audit trail. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
